notes: Oil-and-gas mineral lease/cotenancy dispute (conspiracy to assert adverse title, slander of title damages). 'Lease' here means mineral lease, not residential letting; no bearing on compensated dwelling occupancy.

Marital-property characterization dispute over a home purchase (separate vs. community property) and reimbursement for improvements. Spouses living together in their own home; no letting/lodging of rooms to others.
Landlord's statutory lien priority dispute between a farm landlord's heirs and an attaching creditor over cotton crops. Agricultural cash-rent lease of farmland, not dwelling/room letting.

Suit to remove obstruction from a public alley; the 'rent house' built on the alley and its active renting are cited only as evidence of adverse possession/use against the City, not as an adjudication of the legal character of letting rooms/dwellings. No discussion of lodger status, license vs. lease for occupants, or regulation of boarding.
Trespass to try title; whether a caretaker/ranch tenant's long adverse possession gave constructive notice of repudiation of tenancy to the landlord. Ranch land, not dwelling/room letting for pay.
Construction of a mineral deed's 'lease interest' and overriding-royalty rights. Oil-and-gas leasing, unrelated to residential lodging.
Trespass to try title / adverse possession of timberland, common-source-of-title proof, deed boundary construction. No dwelling letting.
Commercial ground lease of land for a drive-in movie theater; dispute is whether rent abates pro tanto after a partial condemnation taking. Not a dwelling/room letting or lodging-house case.
Whether a reserved mineral 'executive right' to lease survives the grantor's death and passes to heirs. Oil-and-gas leasing power, not residential letting.

Certified question on whether a coastal fishing-regulation statute is an unconstitutional local/special law. No connection to dwelling letting; the 'right to lease' language concerns school-land leasing precedent cited by analogy.
Antitrust suit against oil companies over a marketing 'Code of Practices' governing filling-station leasing/equipment loans. Commercial gas-station leasing, not residential dwelling letting.

Premises-liability suit over a sidewalk depression worn by cars entering a storage garage's driveway; the 'incident of ownership' language concerns a landowner's right of access to a public street, not the right to let dwellings for pay.

Premises-liability case: plaintiff fell through a decayed passageway/awning leading to a vacant upstairs office he mistakenly believed was occupied. Concerns implied invitation to invitees on commercial office space, not residential lodging or boarding.

Zoning/permit dispute over denial of a permit to build a 'drive-in' gasoline filling station near a church, upholding the city's police-power discretion. Commercial land-use regulation, not boarding/lodging-house regulation.
Statute-of-frauds/specific-performance dispute over an oral contract to convey mineral royalty interests in exchange for selling an oil lease at a discount. No dwelling letting involved.

Workers'-compensation case: a discharged oil-lease worker was allowed to keep living in his former employer's rent house in return for looking after machinery. This is an employer-provided-housing/caretaker arrangement tied to employment status, not a compensated short-term letting of rooms/dwellings to lodgers or the public; the dispute is solely whether an employment relationship existed for course-of-employment purposes.

Certified questions on whether a deed-of-trust clause validly converts a foreclosed mortgagor into a 'tenant at will' subject to forcible detainer, and whether a married woman/homestead owner can so bind herself. Concerns the mortgagor's own continued occupancy of her own home after foreclosure, not letting rooms/dwellings to others for pay.

Workers'-compensation course-of-employment case: an employee relocated for work was injured while personally hunting for a rooming/boarding place to stay in. Mentions of a 'rooming house' are incidental to the injured worker's own lodging search, not an adjudication of lodging/boarding-house law.
